$comment: FROZEN BY PHASE 1A / S4 (Automatic Governance Write Review). AUTHORITY = Repository Recovery Authority; this file confers no constitutional authority and legislates nothing. The active hook list is deliberately EMPTY so that no session lifecycle event can trigger an automatic mutation of tracked governance content. RATIONALE: the hook preserved verbatim in $frozen_hook_P1A_S4 fired 00-MASTER/UAKOS-CLOSURE-002/closure_engine.py on SessionStart — automatically, with no operator action and no authorization check of any kind. closure_engine.py writes at :519 (p.write_text, per-artifact) and :746 (closure.json), and 32 of its output files under 00-MASTER/UAKOS-CLOSURE-002/ are git-TRACKED (closure.json itself is gitignored at .gitignore:59). Phase 0 observed it reporting 'wrote 15 artifacts' during a session in which the operator issued no command. AUTHORIZATION MODEL: none existed. The hook was neither gated on a clean tree, nor on a declared authority, nor on any token; SessionStart is not an authorization event and cannot be declined. LEDGER REACH: NONE — verified by source inspection; the engine contains no reference to id-ledger, register.sh, ukb.py or minting, and CLOSURE_SKIP_CORPUS=1 narrowed it further to a repo-only pass. No permanent identity was ever at risk through this path, which is why the remediation is a freeze and not a recovery. WHY FREEZE A BYTE-IDEMPOTENT HOOK: 00-MASTER/UAKOS-CLOSURE-002/ was clean at the Phase 0 baseline despite the 15 writes, so the hook was doing no observable damage. The defect is structural, not observed: an ungated automatic writer into tracked governance content means that on any session in which its output would differ — an input changes, a dependency moves, the engine is edited — tracked registers are silently dirtied before the operator types a single command. The GIT CLEAN INVARIANT would then be broken by session start rather than by any action, and the resulting dirty tree is indistinguishable from a real finding. It also defeats the clean-tree precondition that the Phase 0 D0.4 barrier design places in front of irreversible allocation: a precondition cannot be trusted if an automatic writer can invalidate it between sessions. FAIL-CLOSED PROPERTY: if the hook loader ignores unknown keys, no hook fires because `hooks` is empty; if a loader were strict about unknown keys, this file fails to load and no hook fires either. Both outcomes satisfy the freeze. NOT A DELETION — DETERMINISTIC GENERATION IS PRESERVED: no capability is removed. closure_engine.py is untouched and byte-identical, and the closure workflow remains available on explicit invocation via `CLOSURE_SKIP_CORPUS=1 python3 00-MASTER/UAKOS-CLOSURE-002/closure_engine.py`. It also remains reachable through scripts/generate-prerequisites.sh:65, which verify.sh stage 1b invokes, so the bootstrap path for a pristine clone is unaffected. What changes is exclusively WHEN it runs: on a decision, not on a session. RESTORE: `git checkout -- .kiro/hooks/uakos-closure-002.json` returns this file to its HEAD state byte-for-byte. SCOPE: this freeze is LOCAL ONLY and alters no workflow, no engine and no register.

$frozen_hook_P1A_S4.$comment: The original hook definition, preserved verbatim and inert. Re-arming it is a deliberate act that must not occur until an automatic write into tracked governance content is either brought under a declared authorization model, or the engine's tracked outputs are made unreachable from an ungated trigger (for example by restricting the SessionStart pass to the gitignored closure.json and leaving the 32 tracked artifacts to an explicit render verb).
$frozen_hook_P1A_S4.name: UAKOS-CLOSURE-002 Continuous Ingestion
$frozen_hook_P1A_S4.description: Runs the repository closure workflow (fast repo-only pass) at session start so newly added knowledge is reconciled against Repository Truth and the closure determination is surfaced. Deterministic and idempotent; non-blocking.
